basis: Visual estimate from homes-a-adventurous.png against homes-a-2045.png. Percentages are targets, not measured quantities.

roofMix.reading: New two-storey terraces read as near-continuous blue-black PV roof planes. Flat apartment roofs are planted, with only small paths and terraces. Existing housing beyond remains a mixed grey slate and muted clay roofscape.

wallMaterials.material: warm buff brick or mineral masonry
dark bronze or weathered timber accents

windowRhythm.storeyHeightMetres: 2.9 to 3.1 on terraces; 3.2 to 3.4 on apartment blocks
windowRhythm.windowWidthMetres: 0.9 to 1.2 on terraces; 1.8 to 2.2 per structural bay on blocks
windowRhythm.windowProportion: Terrace openings about 0.55 to 0.70 width:height; apartment glazing about 1.25 to 1.55 width:height
windowRhythm.revealDepthImpression: Strong. Approximately 180 to 250 mm on masonry homes and 300 to 450 mm behind the expressed timber frame on blocks.
windowRhythm.rhythm: One opening per dwelling bay, party-wall breaks and a legible floor band. Avoid a uniform office grid on the homes.

groundCover.hardLandscapeColour: #A69A83 warm buff-grey paving, with #62635D asphalt streets
groundCover.reading: The spaces are garden streets and planted courts, not leftover lawn. Private and communal gardens occupy nearly a third of the visible gaps.

water.visible: Narrow linked rain gardens and stormwater rills along streets, with occasional small holding basins at court ends.
water.channelWidthMetres: 1.5 to 3.5, locally widening to 6 at basins
water.reflectivity: Broken silver-blue sky reflection, #8AA0A3 lit and #324D50 shaded, roughness impression about 0.20 to 0.35 with reeds interrupting the surface.
water.buildability: The exact ornamental complexity in the board is not supportable from current land-class data. Model a few continuous, correctly drained routes rather than every visible glint.

forms: upright lime or hornbeam street tree
trees.density: High within the development, about 30 to 40 per cent canopy cover at maturity; the orchard is denser and regularly spaced.
trees.arrangement: Single and paired avenue trees on streets, one or two large retained trees in each court, orchard rows to the west, and a continuous mixed woodland belt at the rural edge. Deliberately vary crown size and spacing.

sustainableFeatures.PVGlint: Blue-black modules, base #17232D, with sparse desaturated blue-grey glints #91A2AA on upper-left edges. Glint must not turn roofs cyan.
sustainableFeatures.canopies: Only small parking or communal canopies are visible in this shot; keep them secondary to the whole-roof residential PV.
sustainableFeatures.agrivoltaicRows: Not a foreground feature. If caught at the far left edge, use vertical 2 m bifacial panels at roughly 11 m centres with green crop visible between.
sustainableFeatures.glasshouses: Not legible in this camera and should not be added for the sake of this shot.
sustainableFeatures.other: Planted apartment roofs, rain gardens, permeable buff paving and deep garden plots are as important to the reading as the PV.

people/vehicles.people: Tiny 1.7 m figures in pairs and small groups on main paths and court thresholds. At this camera they are one to three pixels and are scale cues, not characters.
people/vehicles.vehicles: A sparse mix of parked cars on streets and a few moving cars, approximately 4.3 to 4.8 m long. Keep shared courts largely car-free.
people/vehicles.scopeNote: The current plan cuts people and cars from aerial delivery. Do not spend geometry budget on them before M7; a restrained sprite or instanced pass could be added later if still needed.

gapsVsPlate.difference: The plate reads as isolated rows and boxes in broad empty green strips; the board reads as a dense network of garden streets, courts and planted thresholds.
gapsVsPlate.modellingAction: Refine parcel infill and internal street/court allocation while retaining the approved 1,030-dwelling total. Add garden polygons and narrow planted thresholds to every home row.

gapsVsPlate.difference: Plate trees are repeated faceted cones with large gaps; the board has mature, overlapping avenue, orchard and woodland crowns.
gapsVsPlate.modellingAction: Introduce four or five crown silhouettes, wider spread variation, clumped woodland edges and continuous street avenues. Preserve enough gaps to see the streets.
gapsVsPlate.system: tree geometry/grade in landcover.js and future.js, plus gv-2045-trees.bin generation
gapsVsPlate.effort: 1.5 to 2 days, covered by in-flight M5

gapsVsPlate.difference: The board's pitched home roofs are almost continuous photovoltaic surfaces; the plate roofs are uniformly near-black and do not resolve as modules.
gapsVsPlate.modellingAction: Raise whole-roof PV allocation to about 60 per cent of visible roof area, keep 45 degree planes, and add module seams plus restrained directional glint.
gapsVsPlate.system: roof shader in facades.js and roof programme in scripts/golden_valley_2045.py

gapsVsPlate.difference: Plate facades are flat beige with shallow punched dots; the board has warm masonry, expressed timber bays and deep shadowed openings.
gapsVsPlate.modellingAction: Tune home and apartment facade branches separately, darken reveals, vary brick/timber by block and keep party-wall breaks visible.
gapsVsPlate.system: futureGeometry in future.js and facade materials in facades.js

gapsVsPlate.difference: No water or rain-garden chain reads in the plate; thin silver lines organise several board streets.
gapsVsPlate.modellingAction: Generate only the principal connected SuDS routes, widen them to a minimum readable 1.5 m and give classified water sky reflection with reed-darkened edges.
gapsVsPlate.system: scripts/golden_valley_2045.py, ground shader in future.js and water treatment in life.js
gapsVsPlate.effort: 1 day, partly covered by in-flight M5

gapsVsPlate.difference: The plate ground is a few flat green classes; the board separates gardens, meadow, buff paving, roads and planting beds.
gapsVsPlate.modellingAction: Add sub-parcel garden and court classes, soften land-cover edges and introduce low-frequency colour and roughness variation without adding fine geometry.
gapsVsPlate.system: gv-2045 land-cover data and ground shader in future.js
gapsVsPlate.effort: 0.5 to 1 day, covered by in-flight M5

gapsVsPlate.difference: The board contains tiny occupants, bicycles and cars that make the streets feel inhabited; the plate is empty.
gapsVsPlate.modellingAction: Defer. If M7 still needs scale cues, instance a very small number of billboard people and low-detail vehicles only on primary routes.
